problem.kicker: The dirty secret of every speaker
problem.title: Your room is ruining your music.
problem.text: Walls, corners, shelves and tables bend the sound before it reaches your ears. Bass booms on one note and vanishes on the next, vocals get boxy, cymbals get harsh. Studios fix this with expensive measurement gear. You now fix it with the phone in your pocket.

demo.sub: Press play and flip the switch. This simulates a typical small speaker in a typical room – boomy bass, boxy mids, harsh highs – and what an AutoVybz correction does to it.

how.title: Three steps. Ten seconds. Zero knowledge.

steps.d: Bluetooth box, soundbar, desktop or party speaker – AUX, USB and HDMI work too.

steps.t: Put your phone where you listen
steps.d: Ear height, bottom mic pointing at the speaker, not in your hand. The in-app guide shows you how.
AutoVybz plays a 10-second test, measures, compensates your phone's mic and saves a perfectly fitted EQ preset.

how.tl_caption: Two independent measurements cross-check each other. Latency is detected automatically, so even laggy Bluetooth speakers measure correctly.

items.d: Smart (gentle bass lift), Neutral, Bass Boost, Harman-style Loudness or your own custom curve.
Fits up to 10 precise filters (or 5 for a lighter touch) and runs them system-wide on every app.
Never boosts bass your speaker can't play. Automatic pre-gain and limiter prevent clipping.
Profiles for popular phones correct the built-in mic. Pro: plug in a USB measurement mic with its calibration file.
Oboe full-duplex audio with raw, unprocessed mic input and a fast native FFT.
Garden, beach, park: max +3 dB boost keeps the loudness, wind and noise are ignored, Bluetooth lag and dropouts are detected, limiter always on.
Equalizer APO / Peace / AutoEq text, JSON, CSV for REW and the native AutoVybz format.
Full Equalizer314 engine: parametric EQ graph, multiband compressor, limiter, presets, AutoEQ for headphones.

items.a: Yes. AutoVybz is 100 % open source under the GPL-3.0. No ads, no in-app purchases, no account, no subscription. If you like it, you can donate – completely voluntary.

items.q: Why only speakers and not headphones?
items.a: A phone mic can't measure what reaches your eardrum inside headphones, and the phone's own speaker sits right next to its mic. For headphones, the Pro area includes Equalizer314's AutoEQ with thousands of headphone profiles.

items.q: Does it work with Bluetooth speakers?
items.a: Yes. AutoVybz detects the Bluetooth delay automatically, so the measurement stays accurate even with laggy speakers.
Android 9 or newer (system-wide EQ uses Android's DynamicsProcessing). Popular phones get a matching mic profile, all others a generic one. For maximum accuracy, plug in a USB measurement microphone.

items.q: Is my audio recorded or uploaded?
items.a: The ~11 seconds of microphone audio are analysed in memory on your phone and discarded immediately. Nothing is saved as audio and the app makes no internet requests.
No. iOS does not allow apps to process the audio of other apps system-wide, so a real system-wide EQ isn't possible there.

items.q: Can it damage my speaker or my ears?
items.a: The test runs at a moderate level after a safety confirmation, and AutoVybz never boosts deep bass below your speaker's limit. Pre-gain and a limiter prevent clipping. Still: start at a low volume and turn up slowly.

items.q: How accurate can a phone mic be?
items.a: Accurate enough for the biggest problem by far: room bass. Above roughly 8 kHz phone mics differ, which is what the compensation profiles and the optional USB mic are for.

js.roast_share: My speaker got roasted 🔥 Vybz score {score}/100 – "{title}". Fix it in 10 s:

corner.d: Corners pile up bass: expect up to +9 dB of one-note boom around 60–120 Hz that drowns everything else.

wall.d: The wall right behind it adds a few dB of bass and smears the midrange with early reflections.

shelf.d: Shelves act like a resonating box: boxy, honky mids around 150–300 Hz and muddy vocals.

table.d: The table reflects sound into your ears a split second late, carving notches into vocals between 300 Hz and 1 kHz.

floor.d: The floor boosts the lows and points the tweeter at your ankles – boomy bass, dull highs.

free.d: Great placement! But room resonances still swing your bass by several dB from note to note.

types.bt: Plus: small drivers fake bass with a hump near 120 Hz and simply stop below ~70 Hz.
types.bar: Plus: soundbars love an aggressive 'dialogue' bump around 2–4 kHz that gets harsh at volume.
types.desk: Plus: little desktop drivers sound thin and the monitor reflections don't help.
types.party: Plus: party speakers ship with a 'smiley face' EQ – boom and sizzle, no middle.
types.hifi: Plus: honestly, good bones! The room is the bottleneck, not your speaker.
